title: NASA Signs
slide_intent: Teach designers to plan exterior signs as a sequence of decisions along a visitor’s route. A driver approaching the site needs a different message and viewing distance from someone looking for a particular door.
strategic_value: NASA can use consistent type and alignment across a facility while allowing the size, material and amount of information to follow each sign’s job.
demonstration: A landscape sheet separates exterior identification from exterior information. Site and building signs share the page with arrows, a map, a parking sign and access warnings.
practical_value: Map the trip from arrival to destination, then test a sign mockup at its intended viewing distance before specifying its material or mounting.

content_islands.name: Planning principles
content_islands.spec: Across the top, explain message brevity, viewing distance, site conditions and flush-left typography.

content_islands.name: Exterior identification
content_islands.spec: Group a–d in a horizontal band. Compare the freestanding site sign, the wall-mounted identifier, the modular contractor sign and separate letters fixed to a building.

content_islands.name: Exterior information
content_islands.spec: Below the dividing rule, align the numbered illustrations with their notes. Show arrows, map, parking and safety messages at sizes suited to their different uses.
